 Learn more On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 9, 2026, Better Home & Finance (NASDAQ:BETR) outlined an operational overhaul to lower fixed costs and push toward core profitability. Investors focused on long-term value need to evaluate whether aggressive expense reductions can stabilize cash flow while high mortgage rates depress loan originations. Three takeaways from the call stand out. 
 1. Management Restructures Operations to Trim Operating Expenses 
 By replacing traditional management layers with software tools, the company aims to reduce quarterly adjusted operating costs to between $45 million and $47 million in the fourth quarter. Cutting corporate overhead helps the business stabilize cash flow while mortgage volumes remain volatile. 
 To that effect, since my return, we have delayered our management and corporate structure by letting go of managers across the company for over $3.5 million of annualized savings.
-- Vishal Garg, Founder and Head of Product, Platform and Innovation 
 2. Shift Toward Home Equity Lines of Credit Drives Higher Yields 
 Home equity lines of credit, or HELOCs, generate six to eight points on gain on sale compared to two to three points for traditional mortgages. Expanding this product lets the lender earn equivalent revenue on smaller loan balances. 
 And so the balances are smaller, but we basically end up making about the same amount of money in revenue on a HELOC as we do on a mortgage.
-- Vishal Garg, Founder and Head of Product, Platform and Innovation 
 3. Proprietary Software Drives Growth in Platform Loan Volume 
 The company's proprietary loan platform, Tinman, originated 57% of third-quarter loan volume, up from 40% a year ago. Shifting volume toward automated platform partners can lower customer acquisition costs, or CAC, by allowing the business to scale without spending heavily on direct advertising. 
 At the same time, the Tinman platform continued to deliver strong year-over-year growth and represented an increased share of our business.
-- Loveen Advani, Chief Financial Officer 
 Looking Ahead 
 Mortgage market headwinds continue to depress refinancing activity, but automated underwriting tools expand broker distribution. The business relies on software automation and third-party partner integration to capture market share while working toward breakeven in adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization). 
 As our new HELOC partnerships and brokerage relationships ramp, our priority is to translate the distribution into funded volume without rebuilding overhead.
-- Loveen Advani, Chief Financial Officer 
 Story Continues Strategic execution now centers on maintaining lower fixed overhead while expanding loan originations through external partners. 
 We have a lot of work ahead, but we have a clear set of priorities: get to profitability, restore growth, bring costs down and get Better 2.0 to sustainable growth and profitability.
-- Vishal Garg, Founder and Head of Product, Platform and Innovation
